title: Improving a presentation: an algebra with retraction and free differentials on the smooth locus
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $A$ an $R$-algebra of finite presentation. There are an $A$-algebra $C$ of finite type over $A$ and a homomorphism of $A$-algebras $\rho:C\to A$ (a retraction of $A\to C$) such that for every $a\in A$ for which $A_a$ is a smooth $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], the localization $C_a$ (at the powers of the image of $a$) is a smooth $R$-algebra and $\Omega_{C_a/R}$ is a free $C_a$-module. (For a presentation $A=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/I$ one can take $C=\operatorname{Sym}^*_A(I/I^2)$ with $\rho$ the projection to degree $0$.)

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07CE (lemma-improve-presentation, line 342) and its proof (C = Sym_A(I/I^2)): clause (2) gives Omega_{C_a/R} free when A_a is smooth; clause (1) gives C_a smooth over A_a when R -> A_a is a local complete intersection (More on Algebra, Definition 07D0), which holds for smooth A_a (Algebra, Lemma 00TA: smooth implies syntomic), so C_a is smooth over R by composition. The node states this combination, which is how the proof of Lemma 07FJ uses 07CE ('C_{x_i} is smooth over k[x_1,...,x_d] with finite free module of differentials').
